angle: Treat AI bets like any other capital allocation: frame the decision, meter the spend, and pre-commit the kill switch.
sourceTitle: ServiceNow CFO: Trillions are being spent on AI initiatives. Are companies asking these 3 key questions?
linkedinPost:
AI spending is exploding. Governance often isn’t.

A recent Fortune piece with ServiceNow’s CFO argues leaders should slow down just enough to ask sharper questions before funding AI at scale. I agree—and I’d add a practitioner’s twist from deployments that actually cleared the ROI bar.

Three questions I see separating value from waste:
1) What decision or workload will this change—and what are we turning off if it works? If nothing will be decommissioned, expect soft savings only.
2) How will we meter the experiment? Define a 30/60/90-day scorecard with 2-3 leading metrics (cycle time, FCR, deflection) and a pre-agreed “stop or scale” gate.
3) What operating constraints are non-negotiable (risk, brand, compliance), and who owns them weekly—not at the QBR?

The finance lens matters: treat AI like capital allocation, not R&D theater. Time-box learning, tie spend to milestones, and pre-commit the kill switch.

If your AI initiative can’t survive those questions, it shouldn’t get budget. If it can, it deserves to scale.

What’s on your 90-day AI scorecard before you release the next dollar? #AIStrategy #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
